doc.title: George Russell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Garbarek and Rypdal's debt to the Concept
summary: Russell and Daughtry discuss Garbarek crediting him as his first teacher and Rypdal's rock career.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: And still are. Here’s one thing that Jan Garbarek had to say about you. He said, “George enlightened me about a different way of playing music, an analytical way which enabled me to go on learning about music on my own.”
Yeah, he’d never studied music – that’s funny – except the Concept.
He’s a great musician who many people appreciate.
He is something.
And many people don’t realize his real creative efforts came out of studying with you, once you took him under your wing.
Well, he had something before he met me. As I said, when I heard him, he was playing like Trane. I thought, how could this little kid here in Norway . . .
Half a world away.
. . . be – sound like Coltrane. But the Concept he embraced.

Yeah, I think obviously he had talent, raw talent, but it really opened him up. He has always, even today, been a very interesting player to hear. He’s got a record out now. I’m trying to think of the name of it. But the larger point I want to make is that I continue to find his approach interesting. One of the reasons I find it interesting is because his explorations are open, and the songs he writes are open. That’s obviously the influence of Lydian, which he is still working and developing to this day. Now I don’t know – I can’t say that that’s all that he does, that’s the only thing that he brings to it, but it’s made a big difference.
He’s never been – how can I put it? – he’s never been quiet about his association with me. He’s always . . .
He’s very proud of it.
Yeah. He’s always been very positive about that and very lovely to say . . .
Very positive, very complimentary.
. . . “George is my first teacher.”
Yes, he has – you’re quite right about that. I’ve heard some interviews that he’s done, and your name has come up in both of the two I’ve heard.
He’s a sweetheart. When I met them, the two or three kids in the band were going with nice women. They all married. He’s married. He has kids. It’s funny how people . . .
That’s part of your legacy out there, George, Jan and Terje.
Terje’s a little wacky, but he’s something. He was very popular in this rock . . .
Milieu?

This rock way of playing. He was at the top of rock guitar playing. Lives on a farm in Norway. I’ve lost touch with the boys. I see them now and then. But they do – the Norwegians and Swedes do recognize the contribution to the music in general and the players.
